interventions.body:
Expert 1 here — the classifier that reads the structured panel and nothing else. My bid:

SUGGESTION: NO BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.34
  uncertainty  +/- 0.16 epistemic (95% band 0.02-0.66); among patients I cannot tell apart the outcome was 0.93 of 1.00 mixed
  reliability  LOW ('discuss' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 55% of the time over the 38 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most, across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, PI-RADS >= 4, no prior biopsy, pmhx_hypercholesterolaemia, suspicious DRE, number of comorbidities. I read 39 variables, all
from the panel — nothing from the mpMRI prose, the PSA trajectory, the previous notes or the
laboratory. Out-of-fold over 91 labelled cases: AUC 0.758, balanced
accuracy 0.625.

The final call is the chair's.

interventions.body:
This patient's situation: prior positive biopsy. My criterion answers DEFER.

The criterion: PSA >= 20 ng/mL in a man with a tissue diagnosis: the next step is staging and treatment, not more tissue. In the labelled series this criterion matched the reading urologist in 5 of 6 cases in exactly this situation.

Like Expert 1, I have read ONLY the visible panel — not the mpMRI prose, the PSA trajectory, the
previous notes or the laboratory panel. Departing from me needs a specific finding from a document
somebody actually opened, named out loud; not a restatement of the panel numbers I already used.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The guideline addresses the risk-adapted matrix for biopsy based on PI-RADS score and PSA density. It states that a PSA-D cut-off of 0.15 ng/mL/cc is used to guide the decision to perform a biopsy.

"linking PI-RADS score (1-2, 3, and 4-5) to PSA-D categories (< 0.10, 0.10-0.15, 0.15-0.20 and > 0.20ng/mL) (Table 5.5) [230]. This risk-adapted matrix table may guide the decision to perform a biopsy."

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
Expert-Structured's suggestion of no biopsy is based on a general panel of variables, but the guideline emphasizes that the decision should be risk-adapted using the PI-RADS score and PSA density. Expert-Cohort's criterion, which focuses on prior positive biopsy, is a specific clinical scenario that the guideline does not override with a simple rule.

WHAT WE STILL NEED
The guideline requires the PSA density value to determine the risk category. The panel shows the PSA density is 2.61 ng/mL², which falls into the highest risk category (> 0.20 ng/mL/cc). The guideline requires the specific prior biopsy status to be known to apply the risk matrix correctly.

interventions.body:
This case hinges on determining the specific details of the prior biopsy and the PSA trend to apply the EAU risk-adapted matrix.

The documents for this session were fixed by EXPERT-TRACE; what I add is the question each one has to answer, and the open questions for the room.

REGISTRAR — pull these up, and answer exactly the question attached to each:
  radiology_report (get_mri_report) -> What is the lesion size and zone, and is there extraprostatic extension?
  psa_trend (get_psa_trend) -> What is the serial PSA value trend (rising, flat, or falling) over time?
  previous_notes (get_previous_notes) -> What was the GRADE of the prior biopsy, and is there a surveillance protocol in place?

OPEN QUESTIONS for this conference — these are what the decision hangs on:
  Q1. What was the GRADE (Gleason/ISUP) of the prior positive biopsy?
  Q2. Is the patient currently on a surveillance protocol with a confirmatory biopsy due?

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (clear). Last value 113.00 ng/mL over 4 points spanning 27 months; velocity +42.01 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 8 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 481.5 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 138.2-1678.4.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-FUSION
interventions.who: Expert 3, Extra-Trees on panel + laboratory + MRI prose; speaks only on documents that were opened
interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report — the laboratory panel was not opened, so that block is imputed and my band is wider for it; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: NO BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.38
  uncertainty  +/- 0.13 epistemic (95% band 0.12-0.64), of which 0.01 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  LOW ('discuss' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 59% of the time over the 29 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the
surveillance history: those are in the notes, and the registrar has to carry them.

data.gist: Expert 3 suggests NO BIOPSY, p=0.38 +/- 0.13, LOW reliability (discuss, fusion_nolab)

interventions.speaker: VERIFIER
interventions.who: second EAU reader; checks against the guideline whether this can be decided yet
interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents retrieved by the registrar—the radiology report, PSA trend, and previous notes—directly address the moderator's open questions regarding the prior biopsy grade and surveillance status.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The panel protocol concluded NO BIOPSY based on the cohort criterion (PSA $\ge 20$ ng/mL) and the lack of a documented prior grade. The retrieved information confirms the rising PSA trend and the PI-RADS 5 score, which support the risk profile used by the cohort criterion.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. What was the GRADE (Gleason/ISUP) of the prior positive biopsy? The registrar reported "PRIOR GRADE: not recorded." Q2. Is the patient currently on a surveillance protocol with a confirmatory biopsy due? The registrar reported "SURVEILLANCE: not recorded."

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The PSA trend (rising from 12.0 to 113.0 ng/mL) is highly relevant as it supports the high-risk classification used by the EAU guideline (PSA density $> 0.20$ ng/mL/cc). The lack of a documented prior grade is a critical missing piece for fully contextualizing the cohort criterion's application.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
Given that the panel protocol's answer rests on the cohort criterion, and the retrieved data confirms a high-risk trajectory, the current recommendation of NO BIOPSY appears consistent with the panel's logic, although the missing prior grade introduces uncertainty.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: defer | MISSING: none
